title: Marriage to Ethel Mayes ends; news of his son's death
summary: Tate says the marriage to Ethel Mayes lasted under a year; their son died the night of his Billie Holiday tribute concert.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And of course, we didn't stay together long. Then I was single like for a couple of years, you know, in between there. We must have stayed together about -- I don't think we stayed together a year, really. But I married her, married her. She was pregnant. I'd get them pregnant and --

-- have to marry them. But I didn't have to marry her, of course. She was a woman, but I went on and married her. And that was my son that I just -- she and I's son that died in July. I don't know if I told you about it. The night I played the Billie Holiday, tribute to Billie Holiday, he died that night and I played anyway.
You mean, you know about it before you went on.

Yeah. He was living in Silver Springs, Maryland. He had everything going for him. He was really -- I had sent him to school. He had gone to school and had all kind of connections, an engineer, and he had bought a beautiful home out in Silver Springs, Maryland, and his oldest son -- it was really a tragedy because his oldest son,

Buddy the third, he's only seven -- called him "Three"-- and he hated to leave his -- the next one is three and a half, the wife is a little younger. So it was really a sad thing. So I buried him on July 2nd and July 3rd, I was off to Nice. I just couldn't sit around home. I had to be with guys and play, you know. And they knew it and everybody was nice to me. And they kept it off my mind.

He was -- he was born in '35? '36? '35, I think. He would be about 40, 44. Thanksgiving, he would be about 45, this coming -- he and my sister's birthday is on Thanksgiving day. I think he would be about 45. He had already made it though. He was -- man, he was -- you know, he was a health bug. (Unintelligible). He didn't smoke, he didn't drink and he stayed on -- he went to the doctor all the time for check-ups, all of the time. And -- but he was feeling fatigued and he went to this doctor and the doctor says, "Now, you know, you're straight." He says, "You'll stay well." He says, "Yeah, but I don't have any energy. I don't feel too good." He said, "Something's wrong." So he checked him out. He said, "Well, I don't find anything."
